transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Dennis Hastert, the former House Speaker who was tied to a child sex abuse scandal, has
died.
NPR's Claudia Grisales reports the Illinois Republican was 84 years old.
The coroner's office in Kendall County, Illinois, said they were notified of Hastert's death
Saturday evening.
The coroner said the Plano, Illinois resident was pronounced deceased at his residence while
in hospice care.
He died of natural causes.
The former lawmaker was the longest-serving Republican Speaker of the House before leaving
Congress in 2007.
In 2016, his political legacy was tarnished after he admitted in court to having sexually
abused teenage boys during his years as a high school teacher and wrestling coach.
He was sentenced to 15 months in federal prison after making hush money payments to cover
it up.
Claudia Grisales, NPR News.
A former Libyan operative charged in connection with a Pan Am flight bombing over Lockerbie
nearly 40 years ago is now scheduled to stand trial starting January 19th.
This morning, a U.S. District Judge set a new date.
It was postponed in August, days before the trial was scheduled to begin then.
Abu Aguila Muhammad Masood Khair Al Marimi is accused of engineering the bomb that took
down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland on December 21st, 1988.
Two hundred fifty-nine people on the flight and eleven people on the ground were killed.
The victims included thirty-five Syracuse University students who were studying abroad.
The British Navy says five oil tankers were struck in major waterways in the Middle East
over the weekend, and PR's Hadil Al-Shalchi has details.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center, which is run by the British Navy,
said a crew was safe and an investigation was underway after a commercial tanker reported
explosions near the Bab al-Mendab Strait.
Bab al-Mendab is an alternate waterway on the Red Sea used to transport oil.
Saudi ships have been targeted there by the Iranian-backed Yemeni Houthi rebels.
In separate incidents, four tankers were struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday
and Sunday, according to the British organization.
One vessel suffered damage to its engine room.
It was unclear who launched those attacks.
Oil has been flowing more steadily in recent weeks as the U.S. military, which maintains
a blockade of Iranian ports, guides vessels across the Strait.
It has yet to recover its pre-war mark.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
Several top congressional Democrats are urging the Federal Aviation Administration not to
roll back a requirement that U.S. airlines must keep epinephrine on their flights in
the event of a medical emergency.
More than a dozen lawmakers, including Senators Chuck Schumer and Tammy Duckworth, sent a
letter to strongly lobby for easy access to a self-administered drug to treat severe allergic
reactions or other medical emergencies.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
The FBI says it has arrested a woman in California on charges of spying on a son of Taiwan's
president.
And PR's Jennifer Pak has more from Beijing.
The FBI says Taiwanese President Lai Qingde's son and his family in the U.S. had their home
and vehicles filmed by California resident Wanying Zhang, who then sent the information
back to her handlers in Beijing.
Beijing regards Taiwan, a self-governing island, as its own.
And it suspects President Lai of pushing Taiwan to declare formal independence.
The California woman Zhang was arrested by the FBI over the weekend at the Los Angeles
airport, just before she was boarding a flight to Shanghai.
NPR's Jennifer Pak reporting, "Huge new data centers have many people wondering who pays
for the upgrades to the electrical grid needed to power these facilities."
And PR's Scott Newman says the answer is not an easy one.
Connor Waldok is chief strategy officer at Grid Status, a company that focuses on providing
electricity market data.
He says the costs to upgrade the grid for A.I. are being shouldered by everyone who
buys electricity.
We're talking tens to hundreds of millions of dollars that are being built by these local
utilities that in many cases are just ultimately going to end up in customers' bills.
He says no one has quite figured out the fairest way to divvy up those costs.
In 2024, Maryland forecast that the cost of A.I. would add as much as $216 a year to the
average customer's bill.
Scott Newman, NPR News.

topics.text: Former House Speaker Dennis Hastert, tied to child sex abuse scandal, dies at 84
Libyan operative charged in 1988 Lockerbie bombing scheduled to stand trial starting January 19th
British Navy reports five oil tankers struck in Middle East waterways over the weekend
Congressional Democrats urge FAA not to roll back epinephrine requirement on U.S. airline flights
FBI arrests California woman for spying on Taiwan president's son and his family
New data centers' electrical grid upgrades are adding costs to customers' electricity bills nationwide
